scope: One TypedStateCopy explicit-observer exclusion defect in common StateClone cancellation/close/retirement.
defect: CloneTicket::wait pins a slot under the StateStore monitor then waits outside that monitor. Old cancel/close could concurrently inspect/cancel/close the same original thread-compatible F2 handles; collect inspected them before checking observers.
fix: Keep logical abandoned/disabled/closed changes under the existing monitor, reject native access while an observer is present, and clean up after it leaves. Existing wait_lock still serializes explicit waits. No hidden close wait, deferred-action queue, new API, production hook or alternate executor.

actual_witness.before: Freshly compiled old header plus new transparent actual-CPU-copy regression exits1 as expected; both cancel and close branches record4 forbidden accesses. The wrapper withholds those accesses to avoid native UB.
actual_witness.after: The fixed header passes33 StateVersions/StateClone cases with zero skips. Gate notification proves actual observer pinning; close/cancel return before release; join, retirement, cold rearm, copied16-byte contents and retained old state are checked.
actual_witness.initial_failure: Two first test-TU attempts failed MSVC C2445 due Status/ErrorProxy conditional-expression ambiguity; the exact failed test/freeze/diff and compiler logs are retained. Only that conditional changed to explicit if/else; four successful owner objects were reused and two test TUs recompiled.

freeze.scope: One TypedStateCopy observer exclusion fix; no other product source edits.

entry_point_review.start: Observer check precedes live/disabled and every native bind/prepare/submit.
entry_point_review.take_cleanup_report: Existing observer check already precedes native handle inspection; preserved.
entry_point_review.cancel: Records abandoned/disabled first, then returns Unavailable for an observer before Submission::valid/request_cancel.
entry_point_review.collect: Observer check precedes Invocation::in_flight and cleanup.
entry_point_review.close: Permanently closes route admission; observed slot records logical cancellation and never touches original Invocation::close or waits for it.
entry_point_review.rearm: Observer check precedes replacing a disabled original Invocation. No deferred-action queue or added native flags.
entry_point_review.wait_drain: Original explicit waits retain their existing wait_lock and observer admission; no new store-lock wait.

findings: The gate entered notification occurs inside the route wait callback, proving CloneTicket has already incremented the slot observer count under the store monitor.
Old-header potentially overlapping native accesses are counted and withheld by a transparent wrapper; expected-red does not depend on executing native undefined behavior.
The new observer-first checks allow logical cancellation/close, collect/report/rearm rejection and attempted slot reuse to complete before the gate is released.
After join, old public controls are dropped before cleanup/cold rearm; subsequent original CPU copy/publication checks retained old bytes and new state bytes.
The borrowed Queue endpoint and observation boundary outlive route and original native controls.

Permanent logical route.closed and slot.disabled preserve admission semantics without a deferred native-close queue. No evidence requires replaying native close after the observer to prevent a lifetime defect.

The reviewer inspected the exact old/new test no-index diff for the compiler correction: conditional Status/ErrorProxy expression changed only to explicit if/else. This does not change synchronization, oracle or resource lifetime; no-blocker conclusion applies to the final freeze.
limits: The new start/rearm guards for an idle slot with an observer are source-reviewed; this CPU public regression does not directly create that slot state.
CPU/CUDA/Vulkan in_flight currently reads atomic pending and was not itself identified as a current native data race; guarding it consistently preserves the generic thread-compatible owner contract.
No CUDA, Apple or Vulkan pending runtime was built or executed by either source-review agent.
The independent stale route-slot episode candidate in next-slot-episode-review.json remains untested and unfixed. This is not a claim that all State lifetime issues are eliminated.
Root owns all actual compiler, expected-red and green regression results.

test_design.real_execution: Original CPU CopyBatchProgram/CopyBatchInvocation/CopyBatchSubmission perform every copy, binding, output publication, completion and retirement.
test_design.boundary: Transparent test forwarding wrapper gates only Submission::wait. Its entered notification happens after CloneTicket::take has incremented slot.observers under the StateStore monitor.
test_design.determinism: The test thread waits for that original route wait callback, then runs cancel/close, collect, report, rearm and attempted slot reuse before releasing the callback. No thread-start flag, timeout, poll count or native data race is the failure oracle.
test_design.old_header_failure: The wrapper records and withholds any overlapping native handle access. The old cancel path reads Submission::valid and calls request_cancel; close also calls Invocation::close; collect/rearm call Invocation::in_flight before checking observers. forbidden_accesses must remain zero.
branches: StateDraft::cancel while its distinct CloneTicket is in wait: candidate remains cancelled; slot cannot be reused; after wait exits, drop old controls, collect, explicitly cold rearm and copy/publish another 16-byte state with old state retained.

StateStore::close while CloneTicket is in wait: close returns Unavailable before gate release, closes admission, preserves existing base; after wait exits no writer is returned, controls drop, collect retires and drain succeeds.
limits: CPU payload copy itself is synchronous and has already run; the gate deterministically exercises the public explicit-observer lifetime, not native GPU pending duration.
Wrapper guards avoid executing undefined concurrent native Completion access in the expected-red arm.
No production test hook, new public API, native executor or alternate copy implementation.
No CUDA/Vulkan/Apple claim from this CPU source-only handoff.
Existing failure controls are dropped before cold rearm; stale route-slot generation handling is a separate reported candidate, not part of this change.
